artikel.titel: Hotter US inflation strengthens the case for a December Fed hike
artikel.text: NORTH AMERICA: US consumer price inflation came in hotter than expected, with headline CPI rising 0.4% month-on-month and core CPI up 0.3%, both a tenth of a percentage point above expectations. No year-on-year rates were published because the government shutdown meant no price data was collected in October 2025

artikel.titel: Hungary’s inflation gives the green light for cuts, but global risks say wait
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Inflation accelerated in October exactly as we expected. Fuel prices and seasonal effects drove the pick-up, while there are still no signs of meaningful second-round effects. Despite the recent easing in external risks, we may not see another rate cut in the coming months

artikel.titel: Europe is selling more into the US AI build-out, but losing market share
artikel.text: AI: European exports of equipment supporting the US AI build-out have risen strongly since 2022, with power and cooling suppliers gaining both sales and market share. But Europe’s share of US imports of AI-related equipment is falling as computing takes a larger slice of the market, where European suppliers have a smaller and declining share

Underneath a thick layer of risk and fear, 2027 could turn out to be a surprisingly benign year for the global economy. At least if politics, (AI) investment, stock markets and central banks fall into place at the right time

artikel.titel: Another year of resilience: 3 calls for the global economy in 2027
artikel.text: Despite a long list of risks, 2027 could deliver a surprisingly benign global backdrop of resilient growth, easing inflation and steady central banks. But political disruption in Europe and mounting fiscal pressures could quickly challenge that outlook

artikel.titel: 5 risks for the global economy in 2027
artikel.text: From AI bubbles to geopolitical breakthroughs, these are the five ways our outlook could go wrong – or right

artikel.titel: Brent at $77/bbl: 3 calls for energy markets
artikel.text: Given the level of uncertainty in energy markets this year and with little sign of a change going into next year, any call on energy markets for 2027 is a low-conviction call. But here are our 3 calls for energy markets for 2027

artikel.titel: Our latest views on the major central banks
artikel.text: EUROPE: Here’s our take on what could be next for the Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, the Bank of Japan and the People's Bank of China over the coming months

artikel.titel: Trade survives, but the battle for control intensifies: 3 calls for global trade
artikel.text: Global trade will remain resilient in 2027, but the focus will shift from tariffs to ownership, technology and investment. While not our base case, an escalation in an EU-China trade war would rank among the most significant risks to global trade

artikel.titel: Solid growth and cooling inflation: 3 calls for the US
artikel.text: NORTH AMERICA: Our base case assumes solid growth, cooling inflation and the Fed hiking once more as Middle East tensions subside. However, if President Trump feels constrained after the midterm elections and hawks within the Administration push for more aggression on Iran, we will face a very different economic outlook. Our bold call envisages an AI revolution
